The open side of the hall on screen right shows a sunlit sea and palms under a pale blue afternoon sky, with no moon, no night sky and no ships in the real view. Remove every barrel, crate, sea chest, sack and piece of storeroom clutter. Only the stain behind Nagoji is at night, so keep it as drawn (the view between a black horse's ears down a moonlit quay, sails far out on the water, a Portuguese warehouse burning), but let its edges bleed softly into the daylit hall instead of sitting on the wall as a framed mural. Keep Nagoji as drawn: seated cross-legged on his woven mat, eyes closed, simple cream collarless shirt and cotton dhoti, bandaged wrists, long curly hair tied back, thick curled moustache, smooth clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud. Leave the daylit sky above the open side, upper right, clear and low in detail for the caption.

decisions.issues: v01 is set in a Portuguese court, not the Travancore coastal hall. Two European soldiers in morion helmets and breastplates hold halberds, and a European grandee in a red velvet robe with a white ruff sits in a carved European chair in the left foreground. An iron shackle ring hangs on the wall. None of this matches the script or the neighbouring hall panels. Nagoji himself is on model and well drawn: seated on his mat, eyes open, cream shirt, bandaged wrists, moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud.
decisions.correction: This is the Travancore coastal hall, not a Portuguese court. Draw no European figures at all: no morion helmets, breastplates, halberds, ruffs, velvet robes, carved European chairs and no iron wall rings. Use a reverse angle from the king's platform, with the open side of the hall on screen right showing the sunlit sea and palms through carved stone pillars, a polished stone floor and a brass standing lamp with open wicks. In the background show only Travancore guards in white cotton with crossed leather belts, holding spears. Draw no foreground figure, or at most a soft, out-of-focus sliver of the king's bare brown shoulder with a cream-and-gold cloth at the lower left edge, with no face and no beard. Keep Nagoji exactly as drawn: seated cross-legged on his woven mat, eyes just opened and looking toward the king at screen left, simple cream collarless shirt and cotton dhoti, bandaged wrists, long curly black hair, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud. Leave the sky in the upper middle and upper right clear and low in detail for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Clean. Varma matches the sheet: cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock crest, bare chest, gold necklaces, Vaishnavite mark, head lifted from the map, eyes narrowed, mouth open. Ramayyan is at screen right: thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth, lips closed, stylus paused on the palm-leaf bundle. The open side of the hall is on screen left. The flag is an unlettered silver conch on red, the guards wear white with crossed belts, the lamp is brass with open wicks, and the map carries no text. Two minor points: Varma's finger rests on the hills rather than the river mouth from 4.5, and the background guards differ in dress from those in 5.5. Open sky between the turban and Ramayyan holds the balloon.

The left-foreground over-the-shoulder figure on a red-and-gold throne reads as the king, but he is off model. He has a full dark beard (Varma has a moustache only), wears a long-sleeved white robe under a red velvet cape instead of being bare-chested in cream and gold, and his turban has no peacock crest. He also fills about 40% of the frame. Nagoji is good: seated on his mat, open bandaged hand in a level gesture, eyes toward the king, cream shirt and dhoti, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud. The guards in white with crossed belts, the brass lamp and the open side with sea on screen right all match page 4.
decisions.correction: Remove the bearded, robed figure on the red throne from the left foreground. The king stays off-panel, or appears only as a soft, out-of-focus bare brown shoulder with a cream-and-gold cloth at the lower left edge, with no face, no beard, no long-sleeved robe, no red cape and no throne. Keep everything else as drawn: Nagoji seated cross-legged on his woven mat in a simple cream collarless shirt and cotton dhoti, bandaged hands, one hand open in a level, measured gesture, eyes toward the king at screen left, long curly black hair, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud. Also keep the carved stone pillars, the Travancore guards in white with crossed leather belts and spears, the brass standing lamp with open wicks, and the open side of the hall on screen right with the sunlit sea. Leave the sky in the upper middle and upper right clear and low in detail for three balloons.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Varma matches the sheet: cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock crest, bare chest, gold necklaces, pearl earrings. His eyes cut sideways with a faint twitch at the corner of the mouth, and his head does not turn. Ramayyan is at screen right in plain white cloth, head bowed, already writing with the stylus, and does not look up. The palm leaves carry no painted writing, the hands are sound, the brass lamp has open wicks, and the open side of the hall is on screen left. Minor continuity points: Varma is seated on a cushioned seat here but stood over the map table in 5.3, and the background guards are bare-chested in red waist cloths rather than the white tunics with crossed belts seen in 5.3. Open sky at upper left takes Varma's line, and open sky at upper centre-right, between the pillars, takes Ramayyan's.

Minor only: one seated courtier at far right wears a short-sleeved cream top rather than going bare-chested; the hall here has dark carved wooden pillars (matching the script) while 6.2 and 6.4 show stone columns. Varma (turban with jewelled peacock crest, spear upright), Ramayyan (thin, receding hair, white cloth, closed palm-leaf bundle with no writing) at screen right, and Nagoji from behind (cream collarless shirt, hair half tied back, small gold stud) all match. Brass lamps have open flames, no glass. Clean lettering space in the sky upper left and on the pale wall above the platform.

Minor: the open side shows palms and a tiled roof rather than the sea, and the visible pillar is plain stone while 6.1 has carved wooden pillars; the throne has lion arms (as in 6.4) rather than 6.1's plain red-cushioned seat. Low angle past the platform edge, open side on screen left, Ramayyan near right matches his sheet, stylus poised over a closed bundle with no script marks, Varma behind and left in the crested turban with spear upright, hands sound. Large clear sky upper left and plain wall upper right for both balloons.

Wrong setting and cast: it shows a Portuguese interrogation room in Goa, not the Travancore coastal hall. A European official in a dark embroidered coat with lace cuffs sits in the foreground at a desk with a scroll and book, two helmeted and breastplated Portuguese guards stand behind Nagoji, and an iron shackle ring hangs on the wall. None of this belongs in the scene, and it contradicts the reverse angle from Varma's platform. Nagoji himself is mostly right (cream shirt, bandaged fists on knees, moustache, clean chin, gold stud), but his hair is loose, not tied back, and his eyes are lifted upward rather than level on the king.
decisions.correction: CORRECTION: This is the Travancore coastal hall of Marthanda Varma, not Goa. Show NO Portuguese or European figures: no seated official in a dark embroidered coat, no lace cuffs, no helmeted or breastplated soldiers, no iron ring or shackle on any wall, no European desk, scroll, book or candlestick. The camera stands at the front edge of the king's low raised platform looking down at Nagoji; the only foreground element may be a sliver of the platform's dark carved wooden edge and the hem of a cream cloth with a gold border, with no seated figure. Behind Nagoji, rows of Kerala courtiers sit motionless on mats, bare-chested in white mundus with topknots and no turbans, under dark rafters, with carved wooden pillars and a brass Kerala oil lamp with open wicks; the long open side of the hall is on screen RIGHT, with palms and bright sea beyond. Keep what worked: Nagoji seated cross-legged on his woven mat, bare-headed, in a collarless cream long-sleeved shirt with the sleeves down to clean white linen bandages on both hands, both bandaged hands closed into fists on his knees gripping the dhoti cloth, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, jaw set. His long curly hair is tied back, and his eyes are level and fixed on the platform, never lifted to the sky. Leave plain wall or rafter space in the upper left and upper centre for three lettering areas, clear of his face and hands.

decisions.issues: Minor: the hall has grey stone columns and a pale marble floor (matching 3.1 and 5.x but not 6.1's carved wooden pillars); Ramayyan wears a tiny gold ear stud although the script says no jewellery; there is an extra palm-leaf desk in the right foreground. Otherwise correct: wide from behind Nagoji (cream shirt, curly hair tied back, bare-headed), Varma in the crested turban speaking, Ramayyan at screen right turning his eyes across to Ibrahim, and Ibrahim at the open-side edge on screen left matching his sheet (white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat over the cream pocketed vest, hands folded, no scar shown since that cheek is not toward camera). Lettering can sit in the sky upper left, the plain stone between pillars upper centre and the wall upper right.

v01 turns the Travancore coastal hall into a Portuguese/European audience. In the foreground are a seated nobleman in a red-and-black velvet robe, a man in a black skullcap and black gown (he reads as a Jesuit or European official), and a carved European chair upholstered in red velvet with brass studs. Behind them stand two soldiers in steel morion helmets and breastplates holding halberds, and there is a table with a map. None of these belong in Marthanda Varma's hall: they break the setting, the cast (Ibrahim alone) and continuity with 6.1, 6.4 and 7.3. Ibrahim himself is good. He matches his sheet (white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat over the cream vest with bulging pockets, white mundu, striped shoulder cloth, sandals) and spreads his hands easily. The sea light comes from screen right, and the pale scar sits correctly on his left cheek (screen right). The sky above him is clear for lettering.
decisions.correction: CORRECTION: This is Marthanda Varma's Travancore coastal hall, not a Portuguese or European room. Show NO Europeans of any kind: no seated nobleman in a red-and-black velvet robe, no figure in a black skullcap or black gown, no soldiers in steel morion helmets or breastplates, no halberds, no carved European chair with red velvet and brass studs, and no table with a map or papers. The camera stands beside the royal platform, and the foreground is empty polished dark floor, or at most the dark carved edge of the platform along the bottom of the frame with nobody on it. Ibrahim is the only prominent figure. At most there may be one small, distant Travancore guard: bare-chested, white mundu, crossed leather belts, a plain spear, no helmet. Match the hall of the neighbouring panels: dark carved wooden pillars, a wooden roof edge, brass oil lamps with open wicks. The open side is on screen right, showing bright sea, the inlet with moored native boats and the red laterite outer wall below. Keep what worked. Ibrahim turns three-quarters toward the camera (toward the platform), standing easy with both hands spread. Keep his costume exactly as before: white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark muted-teal short coat open over the cream vest with bulging patch pockets, white mundu, blue-striped shoulder cloth, sandals. The sea light from screen right falls on his left cheek, showing the thin, pale, healed scar from below the left ear to the jaw. Keep clear open sky in the upper part of the frame for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor issues. (1) The soft background is a carved stone pillar, a stone tower and open sky. It reads more like temple stonework outdoors than the dark carved wooden pillars and roof of the hall, but it is soft and works as a glimpse past the open side. (2) A thin black frame line with a white margin is painted around the image; trim it before placement. Otherwise this is clean. The face matches varma-v1 with the court turban, jewelled peacock-feather crest, pearl earrings and gold necklaces. The head tips back in a laugh, there is no other figure and no text, and the large clear sky at upper right takes the caption.

Minor issues. Varma is standing here after being seated in 6.1 and 6.4; this is plausible as he rises to gesture. A few background guards and standing figures wear white turbans; the prompt has no courtier note, and the seated courtiers are bare-headed. Otherwise this matches the script well. The hall has dark carved wooden pillars, and the open side is on screen left with the inlet, moored boats and red laterite outer wall below. Varma (court turban with jewelled peacock-feather crest, bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth, gold necklaces) sweeps a sound five-fingered hand toward the sea. Ramayyan at screen right matches his sheet: thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth, stylus and palm-leaf bundle, no writing visible. Lamps are brass with open wicks. There is no text. Varma's line can sit in the open sky at upper left (x 0.02 to 0.33, y 0.02 to 0.38). Ramayyan's two lines can sit in the sky and ceiling above him (x 0.70 to 0.93, y 0.0 to 0.2) or carry over into the upper-left sky.

Minor issues. The hall here has pale stone pillars and a cream wall instead of the dark carved wood of 7.3. His gaze runs slightly down toward screen right rather than steeply down. Otherwise this is clean. It is a close shot of Varma alone, and the face matches varma-v1 with the court turban, jewelled peacock-feather crest, pearl earrings and gold necklaces; the expression is unreadable. The open side is behind him on screen left, showing an unlettered red Travancore flag with a white conch. The brass lamp has open wicks, and there is no text. The plain cream wall at upper right (x 0.55 to 0.9, y 0.05 to 0.45) gives ample low-detail space for the off-panel Ramayyan balloon and the caption. The off-panel tail goes to the right edge, toward Ramayyan at Varma's left hand.

Minor issues. The beach sits nearly level with the hall floor, and the red stone outer wall seen in 7.3 does not appear. The pillars are pale stone rather than the dark carved wood of 7.3. Otherwise this matches the script. It is a point-of-view shot from floor level between the pillars of the open side, with no foreground figures. Below are the inlet, moored boats and small figures unloading plain, unmarked sacks and checking nets. The boats carry no flags or marks, and beyond them a flat sea runs to an empty horizon. The brass lamp has open wicks, and there is no text. The upper half is wide open sky (x 0.17 to 0.83, y 0.02 to 0.38) for the two captions.

v01 (the only candidate) is rejected. The king seen from behind at screen left is not Marthanda Varma's court look. He is bare-headed with grey curly hair, has no turban or jewelled crest, and wears a long-sleeved white robe. He sits on a red-velvet, gilded, lion-armed European-style throne. This breaks the chapter 6 occasion rule (turban with the jewelled crest at the formal audience in the coastal hall) and the bare-chested, black-haired Varma of 7.3, 7.4 and 9.2. The two guards wear steel morion helmets, cuirasses, puffed breeches and boots, so they read as Portuguese soldiers standing inside the Travancore hall, when the script calls for Travancore guards in white cotton with dark sashes. A European hilltop castle sits across the water. Smaller points: Nagoji's ear ornament hangs as a small drop rather than a stud, and the bandages stop at the wrists, leaving the hands bare. Nagoji himself (moustache, clean chin, cream collarless shirt, cross-legged on the mat with the open side on screen right) is fine.
decisions.correction: Keep the camera behind the king's shoulder on the platform, the open side of the hall on screen RIGHT, and Nagoji cross-legged on his mat: bare-headed, long curly black hair, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, simple collarless cream shirt, village dhoti, bandaged hands resting on his knees, eyes returning from the open side to the king. Keep the clear sky at upper right for the balloons. Change the king in the near foreground at screen left. He is Marthanda Varma seen from behind, in his formal court look: a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest (visible from behind), black hair (NOT grey), bare brown shoulders and back with one cream-and-gold cloth over a shoulder, and gold necklaces. He sits on a low dark carved wooden seat on a mat-covered wooden platform, NOT a red-velvet gilded European throne. Inside the hall, no figures in European steel morion helmets, breastplates, puffed breeches or boots. If guards appear, they are Travancore guards in white cotton with dark sashes and spears. Better still, show only seated courtiers in loose rows: bare-chested, white mundu, topknot, no turban. Through the open side, show the inlet, moored boats and the red laterite outer wall as in 7.3, with no European castle. Draw Nagoji's ear ornament as a small gold stud flush on the lobe, not a hanging drop. Let the linen bandages wrap his palms and knuckles as well as his wrists.

decisions.issues: Acceptable, with minor points. The present-day Nagoji at the bottom left is larger than the script's 'small' (he fills about the lower-left third), but the memory still dominates. The memory rider's ear ornament reads as a tiny drop rather than a flush stud, though it is negligible at this size. Kanka's far hind leg is lost in the splash. Everything else matches the script. The memory Nagoji wears the rust-red turban, cream tunic and red sash, holds the talwar, has unbandaged hands, a moustache and a clean chin, and rides a black mare with a brown bridle and brass fittings. The other riders wear only white turbans, and there is a saffron pennant. The Portuguese musketeers wear broad hats and buff coats and carry matchlocks, and they break formation with no blood. The Chaul fort and church stand behind them, all in warm stained tones. The present Nagoji is bare-headed in the cream shirt with bandaged hands. There is no text. Lettering: the sepia sky band across the top (about y 0.0 to 0.13) is clear. The sky at top right and the low-detail water just right of the present-day Nagoji (about x 0.33 to 0.52, y 0.75 to 0.92) also work. Both tails go to the present-day Nagoji.

Clean. The frame shows only Keshavrao's eyes and brow over the wet wooden hatch coaming in cold blue storm light, with rain and wind-torn sea behind. His black hair is hacked short and plastered wet. He is beardless with no scar, no ear stud and no other figure. His heavy frown lines make him look a little older than nineteen, but the eyes-only framing carries it. His mouth and faint moustache are hidden by the hatch edge, which the script allows. There is no text. The two captions fit over the storm sky in the upper-left corner (about x 0.03 to 0.22, y 0.05 to 0.35) and the upper-right corner (about x 0.83 to 0.98, y 0.05 to 0.3), clear of the eyes. These areas hold only rain and loose rigging.

v01 (the only candidate) is rejected. The script stages this 'as in 3.4', with the open sea side behind the camera and the closed wall behind the figures. Instead, the sea, sky, palms and sailing ships show through the pillars directly behind Nagoji, which breaks the fixed hall plan and the 3.4 geometry. The guards in the background wear European steel morion helmets, cuirasses and boots, so they read as Portuguese soldiers inside the Travancore court. Nagoji wears a broad red sash at his waist, a commander-look element that is not in his chapter 6 look (village dhoti and simple cream shirt only). His ear ornament is a hanging drop rather than a stud, and the bandages stop at the wrists with the fingers bare. His pose, profile, lean toward the platform at screen left, brass lamps and dark rafters are all good.
decisions.correction: Keep the medium side view and Nagoji's pose. He sits on his woven mat at screen right in profile, leaning in toward the dark wooden platform edge at screen left with one bandaged hand reaching forward. He is bare-headed, with long curly black hair, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a simple collarless cream shirt. Keep the open brass oil lamps on the platform and the dark rafters and open hall space above him for two balloons. The open sea side of the hall is BEHIND THE CAMERA, as in panel 3.4. Behind Nagoji, show the hall's CLOSED inner wall of plaster and dark carved wooden pillars, with no sea, no sky, no palms and no ships visible anywhere in the frame. Remove the red sash: below the shirt he wears only a plain cream village cotton dhoti, with no coloured waist cloth. Draw no figures in European morion helmets, breastplates, puffed breeches or boots. Any background figures are small and soft: seated courtiers (bare-chested, white mundu, topknot, no turban) or Travancore guards in white cotton with dark sashes and spears. Draw his ear ornament as a small gold stud flush on the lobe, not a hanging drop. Let the linen bandages wrap his palms and knuckles as well as his wrists.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate) is rejected. A large foreground figure at screen right, seen from behind, wears an exact duplicate of Varma's cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest and his pearl earring. It reads as a second king. The man Varma is watching should be Nagoji, who is bare-headed, so this is a cloned principal and the beat is wrong. The rest is good. The open side is on screen left, with a kingfisher on the parapet and waves on the sand below. Varma matches his sheet: cream-and-gold turban with the crest, bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth and gold necklaces. He sits on the mat-covered platform with his spear butt on the mat and two small motion ticks. There are open brass lamps, an unlettered conch banner, and clear wall space at the upper middle for the balloon.
decisions.correction: Keep everything except the right foreground. Keep the open side of the hall at screen left, with the small bird on the parapet and waves breaking on the sand below. Keep Marthanda Varma seated on his dark carved seat on the mat-covered wooden platform in his formal court look: cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest, bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth over one shoulder and gold necklaces. He taps the butt of his upright spear on the mat, shown by two small motion ticks. Keep the open brass oil lamps, the unlettered silver-conch-on-red banner and the plain wall beside his head for the single balloon. REMOVE the large foreground figure at screen right. No second turbaned figure and no other peacock-feather crest may appear anywhere. Varma is the only person in frame. The man on the mat is off-panel beyond the right edge, and Varma's eyes look steadily toward that right edge. If anything of Nagoji is shown, it is only the edge of his woven mat at the lower-right corner, never a head or turban. Fill the right side with the hall's polished floor, pillars and wall in the same afternoon light.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate): the man on the mat in the foreground wears a rust-red turban and a red sash and has a full beard. That is the commander look leaking in, not ch6 Nagoji (bare-headed, cream shirt, clean-shaven chin). The guards wear European steel morion helmets. A Baroque church with a cross stands on the hill beyond. Ramayyan sits at floor level with the mat, not on the platform above it. Ramayyan himself (face, white cloth, palm-leaf bundles, stylus, open brass lamp) is good.
decisions.correction: Show Ramayyan ALONE in frame. He sits cross-legged behind his low wooden table on the raised wooden platform of the coastal hall (dark carved wooden pillars, the long side open with sea light from screen left). His head is turned down toward screen right as he speaks to a man on the mat below, and that man stays entirely OUT OF FRAME. Draw no foreground or over-the-shoulder figure, and no turbaned, sashed or bearded man anywhere. Keep Ramayyan's face, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundles, stylus, open-wick brass lamp and gesturing open hand exactly as in the previous attempt. Any background guards wear white mundu with crossed leather belts and are bare-headed or in plain white cloth turbans, never metal helmets. The view through the open side shows only the inlet, moored boats, coconut palms and the rough red stone outer wall: no church, no cross, no European building. Keep the upper third of the frame as plain sky or dark rafters, with room for three lettering areas.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Distant Mediterranean-style villas and two campanile-like towers sit on the far shore at screen left; they are small and soft, and coastal churches are plausible here. One seated background courtier wears a white turban instead of the bare topknot seen at 9.5. Varma stands at the rail here but is enthroned at 9.5. Everything required is right: Varma's face matches the sheet with the cream-and-gold turban and jewelled peacock-feather crest, and he gives a thin smile with his eyes down toward the mat. Ramayyan is thin, receding, in plain white cloth with no jewellery, amused, at screen right. The open side is on screen left. The plain wall upper right and the sky upper left take the two lines.

v01 (the only candidate): the foreground man below has a thick dark beard, a dirty stained shirt and an iron collar with a hanging chain. These are captivity props from ch2-3, and they contradict ch6 Nagoji (clean-shaven chin, no irons, clean cream shirt). The framing is a medium over-the-shoulder shot of a standing Ramayyan, not the scripted tight shot. Ramayyan himself (face, faint amused smile, white cloth, ledger, stylus) is good.
decisions.correction: Make it a TIGHT head-and-shoulders close-up of Ramayyan ALONE, seated at his low table on the platform. He looks down toward screen right at a man below who stays entirely OUT OF FRAME. Draw no foreground figure and no back of a head, and no chains, iron collar or shackles anywhere. Keep his face, faint amused smile, sharp eyes, receding hairline with curly hair at the back, plain white cloth, stylus and bound palm-leaf ledger exactly as in the previous attempt. Keep the plain plastered wall and dark wooden rafters behind him, with sea light from screen left, and leave the upper third of the frame clear for two lettering areas.

decisions.issues: Minor only. The hall pillars and balustrade are carved grey stone, not the established carved wooden pillars. The laterite bluff is taller than 'low' and carries a fort; its flags are the correct unlettered silver conch on red. Everything required is right: Varma is in profile in the left third facing screen right, with the turban and jewelled peacock-feather crest, gold necklaces and the sheet's face. A clear strip of wet sand runs between a red laterite bluff crowned with coconut palms and the sea, filling the right two thirds. A large clear sky upper right takes both lines. Ramayyan is off panel at the king's side, behind Varma, so his tail goes to the left edge.

Minor only. The camera is at seated eye level, not high. Ramayyan sits on a carved chair beside the throne rather than at his low table. Nagoji's ear stud is hidden by his hair. Everything required is right: the shot is from the entrance end with the open side on screen left. Nagoji is bare-headed, with long curly hair, a thick moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a cream shirt and dhoti, and a bandaged wrist, kneeling on his mat. Varma is on the platform in the turban and jewelled peacock-feather crest. Ramayyan, in plain white cloth with no jewellery, is at the king's left hand (screen right) and points toward Nagoji with his ledger. The courtiers are bare-chested with topknots. The banner is the unlettered conch on red, and the lamps are open-wick brass. The plain wall at upper centre takes both lines.

v01 puts a European on the platform: the figure in the foreground chair is a bearded man in a red-and-gold doublet with a ruff collar and black boots, sitting on a European high-backed chair. A second European in black stands behind him. Portuguese soldiers in morion helmets and breastplates guard both sides of the hall. The scene reads as a Goa audience, not Marthanda Varma's coastal hall in Travancore, and it contradicts 10.2, where Varma sits in his crested turban on a lion-armed Kerala seat. Nagoji himself is good: bare-headed, curly hair, curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, cream shirt, dhoti, bandaged hands, barefoot and unarmed, with the open side of the hall on screen right.
decisions.correction: The platform in the near foreground belongs to Marthanda Varma of Travancore, so draw NO European anywhere in the frame: no ruff collar, no doublet, no boots, no European high-backed chair, no bearded European courtier, and NO Portuguese soldiers in morion helmets or breastplates. From just behind and beside the low Kerala platform, show at most a sliver of Varma at the near left edge: the back of his cream-and-gold turban with its jewelled peacock-feather crest and his bare brown shoulder with gold pearl necklaces, on a carved wooden Kerala seat with gilded lion armrests, with an open-wick brass oil lamp. Otherwise show only the bare platform edge. The only other figures are two or three Travancore guards standing back by the pillars, in white mundu with crossed leather belts, bare-headed with topknots. Keep everything that worked: the carved stone pillars and the open side of the hall on screen right with palms and the sea beyond, and Nagoji standing barefoot alone on the stone floor a few paces before the platform, straightening. He is bare-headed with long curly black hair, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold ear stud, in a collarless cream shirt and white dhoti, with both hands and wrists bandaged, unarmed. Keep the open sky in the upper right, clear for one balloon.

decisions.issues: v01 adds a large over-the-shoulder figure in the lower-left foreground, seen from behind. He wears a cream-and-gold turban with a peacock-feather crest, the same as the king's, and a shawl with a red border. This makes a second crowned-looking man in the shot. The script calls for a two-shot with Nagoji out of frame, and the courtier rule says no turban. Varma (turban and crest correct for the audience, spear, pearls) and Ramayyan (thin, receding hair, plain white cloth, palm leaves and stylus, at the king's left hand on screen right) are otherwise good, and the open side of the hall is correctly on screen left.
decisions.correction: Remove the foreground over-the-shoulder figure entirely. This is a two-shot with NO third person in the frame. No second turban or peacock-feather crest may appear anywhere: only Varma wears one. Varma's lowered gaze goes down and out of frame past the lower left edge, toward the man below, who is not drawn. In the near foreground there is only the empty stone floor and the edge of the platform. Keep everything else that worked: Varma seated on the carved seat with gilded lion armrests, in the cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest, bare-chested with pearl necklaces, gold armlets and his spear, his face matching the sheet. Keep the open side of the hall on screen left, with pillars, sky and palms. Keep Ramayyan seated at the king's left hand on screen right: thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus, his head turned slightly toward the king and his lips parted as he translates quietly. Keep the open-wick brass lamps. Leave the plain wall at upper right, the sky at upper left and the bare floor at lower left clear for three lettering areas.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Ramayyan and Nagoji walk nearly side by side rather than Ramayyan clearly ahead, but his open-hand 'Come' gesture carries the lead. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small gold bead at the lobe, the same as on his sheet, and reads as a stud. The whitewashed, red-tiled houses across the bay are small and plausible for the coast. For lettering, use the open sky upper centre and right (between Nagoji's head and the right pillar) for Ramayyan's balloon, and the sky upper left above the fort for the caption.

The art carries a painted thin black frame line with a cream margin about 16 px in from every edge. Crop about 18 px off each side before placement. The bandaged right hand rests on the dhoti waist just beside the knot rather than on it, which still reads as the beat. There is no sword, scabbard, sash or belt. The background steps, sea, sails and the town on the far headland are softened as required. The open sky in the upper right (about x 0.57 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.32) takes both italic captions.

v01 is otherwise excellent: a wide strip with Nagoji from behind at the top of the steps, his head turned to screen right in profile (moustache, clean chin, gold stud), cream shirt and dhoti, his right hand bandaged and resting on his hip with no sword or sash. Ramayyan is small at lower left going down the steps with his palm leaves, there is a beach with fishing boats and the coastline running up to the right, and the open sky is free for the caption. But Nagoji's LEFT hand, hanging at his side, is bare with no bandage. This breaks the chapter 6 bible row (hands still bandaged) and contradicts 10.3 two panels earlier, where both of his wrists and hands are wrapped.
decisions.correction: Both of Nagoji's hands must be bandaged. Wrap his LEFT hand and wrist (the arm hanging relaxed at his side, on screen left of his body) in the same white cloth bandage as the right hand resting on his hip, matching 10.3, where both of his wrists and hands are wrapped. Keep everything else exactly as it was: the wide 3:1 strip; Nagoji seen from behind standing at the top of the stone steps, bare-headed with long curly black hair, his head turned to screen right in profile showing the thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and small gold ear stud; his collarless cream shirt with the sleeves rolled and his white dhoti; his bandaged right hand resting on his hip at the dhoti knot, with NO sword, scabbard or sash. Keep Ramayyan small at lower left in plain white cloth with his palm-leaf bundle, already going down the steps; the beach below with fishing boats; the sea and the coastline running up to the right with the fort on the far headland; and the open sky across the upper left and centre, clear for the caption.
